title: Complaint of Dr. Morton H. Smith v. Western Carolina Presbytery
disposition_detail: Issues 2 and 5 were sustained; Issues 1, 3, and 4 were not sustained. The August 7 congregational actions and related Presbytery proceedings were voided. Linton’s and Pellom’s calls remained undissolved, Neville was not called, and—absent subsequent congregational action—the prior Session composition remained.
first_summary: The complaint challenged Presbytery’s commissions and its response to a canceled congregational meeting. The SJC upheld the Inman Commission because a Session may reference limited duties without congregational consent. It sustained the challenges to Presbytery’s consideration of the August 7 meeting and appointment of the Sealy Commission because the Session had validly canceled the meeting, leaving no valid dissolution request. Related actions were voided, while Presbytery’s criticism of the cancellation and refusal to issue a BCO 40-5 citation were upheld.
summary: The complaint challenged Presbytery’s commissions and its response to a canceled congregational meeting. The SJC upheld the Inman Commission because a Session may reference limited duties without congregational consent. It sustained the challenges to Presbytery’s consideration of the August 7 meeting and appointment of the Sealy Commission because the Session majority had validly canceled the meeting. Linton’s and Pellom’s calls therefore remained undissolved and Neville was uncalled, absent later congregational action. The SJC also upheld Presbytery’s criticism of the cancellation as unwise and its refusal to issue a BCO 40-5 citation.

sources.locator: printed pp. 170–173, lines 325–408; adoption and vote at lines 594–598
sources.supports: Case identity, five issue judgments, adopted reasoning, voiding of actions, qualifications, and SJC adoption.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: Case 2008-15 and its five judgments appear at lines 325–341 (printed pp. 170–171); the full SJC amended the Panel draft, lines 594–598.
evidence_notes.dispute: Smith’s specifications challenged the Reference, August 7 requests, criticism of cancellation, refusal of a BCO 40-5 citation, and Sealy Commission, lines 263–277 and 329–339.
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: The Reference required no congregational consent, lines 343–366. The canceled August 7 meeting was illegitimate, and its actions and related proceedings were voided, lines 370–386 and 406–408.
evidence_notes.qualifications: Cancellation was constitutional but could still be judged unwise; the citation claim lacked evidence of credible reports, lines 388–404. Restoration of the former Session was conditional on no later congregational action, line 386.
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: Case 2008-15 incorporates no other decision. Cases 2009-01 and 2009-03 instead were later answered by reference to it, lines 572–592.

source_limits: The supplied file combines six cases, but it contains the complete operative judgment and reasoning for 2008-15. No external authority was used.

score_reasons.concrete_dispute: Identifies the challenged commissions, canceled meeting, criticism, and citation refusal.
score_reasons.decision: States both sustained issues, all rejected issues, and the practical effect of voiding the actions.
score_reasons.decisive_reason: Explains both the permissible Reference and the absence of a valid request after cancellation.
score_reasons.distinctive_value: Preserves the distinctions between constitutional and wise action and between a limited Reference and takeover of governance.
score_reasons.fidelity: Separates Presbytery’s actions from the SJC’s judgments and preserves the conditional qualification about later action.
score_reasons.economy: Retains only facts needed to explain the mixed result and relief.

verification_notes: Rechecked all five judgments against lines 329–339 and the remedies against lines 376–408. The corrected summary adds the Session-majority basis, the status of the three officers, and the qualification concerning later congregational action.
